claim: “Neither and nor belong to both the class of coordinators and that of connective adverbs (again, see Ch. 15, §2.4, for discussion).”
evidence_summary: Ch. 15, §2.4, p. 1308, the section cited: “The determinative neither, like both and either, functions as a determiner in NP structure or as a marker in correlative coordination”, and “In addition, it is an adverb functioning as connective adjunct”. Page 1307: both and either “are clearly distinct from the coordinators”. Ch. 5, p. 389: “Neither functions likewise as determiner (neither parent) or marker of an initial coordinate”. The inventory of coordinators on p. 1293 doesn’t include neither.
finding: High confidence for neither, which Chs. 5 and 15 treat as a determinative and an adverb. The defence that p. 778’s “class of coordinators” loosely means items that mark coordination fails, since p. 1307 sets these determinatives apart from the coordinators. For nor the wording is partly right: pp. 1309–1310 make it a connective adverb for speakers who accept and nor, and a coordinator for many others.
proposed_wording: Neither is both a determinative and a connective adverb, and nor a coordinator and, for some speakers, also a connective adverb (again, see Ch. 15, §2.4, for discussion).

evidence.passage: §19, p. 778. “Neither and nor belong to both the class of coordinators and that of connective adverbs”
evidence.example: Ch. 15, p. 1308 [46] neither player, neither Kim nor Pat. Ch. 5, p. 389.
evidence.establishes: The section cited puts neither in the determinative and adverb categories, not among the coordinators.
evidence.note: Local source (working note, unpublished draft or local copy); not online.
